title: Please tell me people get this reference 😅. “I Became We” is playing ...
transcript: What if the J G. Wentworth Choir narrated your life? This was, I imagine, the question on Mona Pirnot’s mind when she wrote her new play, I became we, a solo first person monologue performed by a classical 16 person choir. And instead of singing about what to do if you need cash now, they are instead narrating her life as a woman in her mid thirties trying to figure out what she actually wants out of life. It creates this really interesting juxtaposition where these somewhat mundane aspects of life are given this gravitas to it through the music. Things like gossiping with a friend or scrolling through Zillow. But then you also have this character grappling with some big decisions. Things like, should I have a kid? Should I buy a house? What if my partner doesn't agree? These are weighty questions that are made even weightier through the music. There's something very captivating about it all. It really draws you in. And while I'm sure that would be the case if it was just a solo performer, the music and choir does give it this epicness that I don't think you could get with just one person. It also really emphasises the universality of this story, almost as if 16 people are having the exact same experience at the exact same time, all of different ages, ethnicities, genders. And if not only for the sheer novelty of it, I became we is going to be a Broadway Ben recommendation
